blocks.text: 1. Few-Shot Prompting
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581443-41925552.png
Citation Prompting's closing recap pointed forward here. Few-Shot Prompting covers how examples in the prompt shape the model's response style, shifting from written rules to concrete demonstration.
It covers including a small number of example question and answer pairs directly inside the prompt.
2. Showing Rather Than Telling The Model
Citation Prompting and earlier topics relied on written instructions describing the desired behavior.
Few-shot prompting shows the model concrete examples of that behavior instead.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","How it teaches behavior"],"rows":[["Written instructions","Describes the desired behavior in words"],["Few-shot examples","Demonstrates the desired behavior directly"]]}

blocks.text: 3. What An Example Pair Actually Looks Like

blocks.alt: What An Example Pair Actually Looks Like
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581443-71661382.png
A single example pairs a sample question, sample retrieved context, and the ideal answer together.
This demonstrates exactly the format and style the model should follow.
4. Demonstrating Citation Style Through Examples
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581444-175842668.png
Citation Prompting covered citation format consistency; an example answer that correctly cites its sources teaches that pattern by demonstration.
This often works more reliably than a written description of the same rule alone.
5. Demonstrating How To Handle Missing Information

blocks.alt: Demonstrating How To Handle Missing Information
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581444-828594913.png
System Prompting covered handling missing information explicitly; an example showing the correct "I don't know" response reinforces that exact behavior.
This gives the model a concrete template for that specific, tricky case.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Including one example where the ideal answer says the context does not contain enough information reinforces that specific behavior far more concretely than a written instruction alone.

blocks.text: 6. Token Cost Of Included Examples
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581444-383977128.png
Token Budgeting covered how every part of the prompt takes space; every included example likewise consumes real token budget.
More examples mean less remaining space for the actual retrieved context.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Adding five full example pairs to every single prompt can consume hundreds of tokens before the actual retrieved context and query ever appear, a real cost against a finite token budget.

blocks.text: 7. Choosing Representative Examples
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581444-485556339.png
Poorly chosen examples can teach the model the wrong pattern just as effectively as good ones teach the right one.
Each included example needs to be deliberately representative of the desired behavior.
8. Few-Shot Versus Zero-Shot
Zero-shot prompting relies purely on written instructions with no examples at all.
Few-shot prompting trades extra tokens for more reliably demonstrated behavior.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Prompting style","Tradeoff"],"rows":[["Zero-shot","No extra tokens, relies purely on written instructions"],["Few-shot","Extra tokens, but more reliably demonstrated behavior"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Few-Shot Prompting Is Worth The Added Tokens

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Few-Shot Prompting Is Worth The Added Tokens
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581444-881401062.png
Tasks needing a specific, hard to describe format benefit most from few-shot examples.
Simple, easily described tasks, by contrast, often work well with instructions alone.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Including so many examples that little token budget remains for the actual retrieved context.
Choosing examples that do not actually represent the desired behavior.
Forgetting to include an example demonstrating the correct handling of missing information.
Using few-shot examples for simple tasks that would work just as well with plain instructions.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Few-shot prompting includes example question and answer pairs directly inside the prompt.
It shows the model concrete examples of desired behavior rather than only describing it.
An example pairs a sample question, sample context, and the ideal answer together.
Example answers that correctly cite sources teach that pattern through demonstration.
An example showing the correct uncertain response reinforces that specific behavior.
Every included example consumes real token budget, leaving less room for retrieved context.
Poorly chosen examples can teach the wrong pattern just as effectively as good ones teach the right one.
Few-shot prompting trades extra tokens for more reliably demonstrated behavior than zero-shot.
